# Grida FX

> Grida FX is a workflow engine for generated assets (images, video, audio, 3D models, structured
> text) and ordinary local code. You describe steps in a YAML workflow; FX plans the run offline
> with its price, runs only what changed, caches every result by content, reserves every paid call
> against a ceiling, and records how each result was made. The command is `grida fx`.

Version: 0.6.1

This file is the reference for people and coding agents using FX: what exists, how to write it,
and how to run it, as complete recipes. It is kept by hand and checked in CI against the engine
of the release it names: every recipe below is planned, every `grida fx` command is checked
against the command's own help, and every link resolves. When it and the guide, the README or a
skill disagree, trust this file. Only the contracts in `spec/` (normative) and the engine itself
rank above it. An installed FX may be older or newer than the version above: `grida fx --version`
says which you have, and `grida fx --help` and `grida fx <verb> --help` are always right for it.

## Rules for agents

- **Plan first; it is free.** `grida fx plan <workflow>` never calls a provider. Show the user its
  steps and estimate before any run that may spend.
- **Spending is the user's call.** `--live` admits paid calls. Run it only with the user's go and an
  agreed ceiling (`--max-usd`). A run on the user's own Codex or Grok Build needs no ceiling but
  spends their subscription: ask for that too.
- **Keys are the user's.** Never read, print, write or commit `.env` or a key. Ask the user to set
  keys; check what FX found with `grida fx doctor`. FX never writes provider credentials.
- **Discover, don't guess.** `grida fx nodes`, `grida fx nodes <type>`, `grida fx schema <target>`
  and `grida fx --help` list what this installation has.
- **Ask before changing a route.** The route is part of a step's identity: a new route draws anew
  and earlier results don't carry over.
- **`runs/` and `.fx/` belong to FX.** Read runs with `grida fx inspect` or the SDKs; never edit
  them by hand.
- **Show the live viewer.** When the project service is running (`grida fx status --json`), give
  the user the URL `plan --open` or `run` prints instead of describing renders yourself.
- **Don't retry paid calls yourself.** The engine is the only retry owner (at most 6 attempts per
  call). A failed run is resumed or run again; cached work is not redone.

## Install and check

```sh
npm install -g grida   # the grida command, with FX as `grida fx` (Node.js 24 or later)
pip install grida      # the Python SDK, for nodes and builders in Python (Python 3.11+, brings Pillow)
npm install @grida/fx  # in a project: the SDK for nodes and builders in TypeScript (Node 24+ to host them)
grida fx doctor        # the engine, Python, Node, keys, Codex/Grok Build and routes FX found
```

- `npx grida fx <verb>` works without a global install. `grida-fx` (from `@grida/fx`) and
  `python -m grida.fx` (from the Python package) are the same FX with the same verbs, project
  files, cache and records; `--version` tells installations apart.
- Platforms: macOS, Linux (glibc 2.28+), x64 and arm64; Windows through WSL 2.
- **Python is needed** for your own Python nodes and builders, and for the built-in local types
  (`image.resize`, `image.crop`, `image.pad`, `image.mirror_repeat`, `image.check_alpha`,
  `image.check_size`, `json.merge`, `files.copy`, `package`). FX picks `GRIDA_FX_PYTHON`, else the
  workflow project's `.venv`, else the `.venv` of the project you run from, else the SDK's own
  Python, else `python3` on `PATH`; older than 3.11 is refused.
- **Node 24+ is needed** for TypeScript nodes, builders and stand-ins (Bun and Deno cannot host
  nodes). FX picks `GRIDA_FX_NODE`, else the Node running `grida fx` or the SDK, else `node`.
- Paid built-in types (`image.generate`, `structured.generate`, …) and `fx/select@1` run in the
  engine and need neither.

## A project

```sh
npx grida fx init my-assets       # a starter project in a new or empty folder; installs and starts nothing
cd my-assets
grida fx start --background       # the local viewer at http://127.0.0.1:8787/ (optional)
grida fx plan icon -- --name "copper lantern"
```

`init` writes `fx.yaml`, `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, the FX agent skills in `.agents/skills/`,
`.gitignore`, `.env.example` and `workflows/icon.yaml`. `grida fx init --list-templates` lists
templates; `--template NAME` picks one. In a folder that already has an `fx.yaml` it only checks it;
any other non-empty folder is refused (write `fx.yaml` yourself to adopt an existing repository).

```
my-assets/
  fx.yaml          # project settings: the folder that holds it is the project root
  workflows/       # workflow files (searched recursively for `grida fx run <id>`)
  nodes/           # your own node types (optional)
  prompts/         # prompt templates (optional)
  runs/            # one folder per run          (FX writes it; keep out of git)
  .fx/cache/       # content-addressed results   (FX writes it; keep out of git)
  .fx/service/     # local service state         (FX writes it; keep out of git)
```

```yaml
# fx.yaml
fx: project/v1
budget:
  max_usd: 10                       # ceiling for any one run; --max-usd overrides it
routes:                             # the model for each capability, where a step names none
  image.generate: openai/gpt-image-2.5-sunburst@gg
  structured.generate: { route: openai/gpt-5.6-sol@gg, concurrency: 4 }   # at most 4 calls at once
# route_tables: [routes/prices.yaml]   # your own route tables (fx: routes/v1), read after the built-in one
# workflows: [workflows, ../tools/art] # where a workflow id is looked for (replaces the default)
# cache: ../shared-cache               # share a cache across projects
# sources: [acme_lib]                  # packages whose source counts toward your nodes' identity
```

A path that starts with `./` or `../` in a workflow (`uses:`, `prompt:`, `schema:`, a file in
`with:`) is relative to the project root, the folder of the nearest `fx.yaml` above the workflow,
whichever file it is written in. Absolute paths are refused.

## The workflow file

```yaml
fx: workflow/v1          # required
id: gallery              # required: stable; names runs/<id>/ and `grida fx run gallery`
title: Gallery           # required
description: …           # optional
inputs:  { … }           # what a caller supplies
tables:  { … }           # constant lookup tables
let:     { … }           # named expressions
budget:  { max_usd: 12 } # this workflow's default ceiling
assert:  [ … ]           # plan-time checks
steps:   { … }           # required: the work
outputs: { … }           # what the workflow promises
```

Three ideas govern everything:
- **A step is a pure function of what it declares.** It sees only what is wired to it.
- **Results are kept by content.** A step runs again only when its node type, `with:` values,
  input bytes, upstream results, route or take changed. Renaming or reordering steps reruns
  nothing. Paid calls are also cached by their exact request.
- **Order comes from wiring.** Steps run as soon as their inputs exist, in parallel.

### Strict YAML

FX reads a strict YAML subset with one meaning everywhere. Refused with "quote it": `yes`, `no`,
`on`, `off` (any case), `True`/`FALSE`/`Null`, leading-zero numbers (`017`), `0x1F`, `1_000`,
`16:9`, `.inf`, dates (`2026-10-05`). Write `"16:9"`, `"on"`. Duplicate keys, anchors, aliases and
tags are refused. `1024x1024`, `y` and `n` are plain strings.

### Inputs

```yaml
inputs:
  name:     { type: string, description: "What the item is" }
  count:    { type: integer, default: 4, minimum: 1, maximum: 48 }
  ratio:    { type: number }
  draft:    { type: boolean, default: false }
  poster:   { type: file, kind: image }            # kind: image, audio, video, text/markdown, …
  sprites:  { type: files, kind: image, glob: true }   # many files, keyed by file stem
  tags:     { type: list, items: { type: string }, unique_items: true }
  layers:                                          # a list of objects: `items` is a field map
    type: list
    max_items: 32
    items:
      id:   { type: string, pattern: "^[a-z0-9_]+$" }
      file: { type: file, kind: image }
  canvas:                                          # a nested object: nest fields
    width:  { type: integer }
    height: { type: integer }
  voices:   { type: map, values: { voice_id: { type: string } } }
```

Keywords are snake_case (`max_items`, `min_length`, `unique_items`). An optional input with no
default is `null`. `grida fx schema <target>` prints the JSON Schema they compile to. Give inputs
as kebab-case flags after `--` (`-- --max-entities 24 --poster art/p.png`), or in YAML files with
`--inputs file.yaml` (repeatable, later wins; paths inside are relative to that file). Lists and
maps need a file; a `files` input also takes a quoted glob.

### Steps

```yaml
steps:
  draw:
    uses: fx/image.generate@1          # a built-in type, ./nodes/x.py#name, ./nodes/x.ts#name,
                                       # or ./workflows/other.yaml (a workflow as one step)
    with: { prompt: "A ${{ inputs.name }} icon", size: 1024x1024, background: transparent }
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `with:` | the node type's inputs and settings |
| `if:` | run only when true (plan-time values decide in the plan; run-time values make it *maybe*) |
| `needs:` | order after steps without reading them (rare) |
| `for_each:` `as:` `key:` `max:` | repeat per item; `max:` is required when the list comes from a step |
| `matrix:` | repeat over every combination: `{ eye: [...], mouth: [...] }`, read as `matrix.eye` |
| `steps:` | a group: nested steps that repeat or regenerate together |
| `judges:` `on_reject:` | this step judges another (below) |
| `regenerate:` | on a group: redo it until accepted, `{ max: 3, until: "${{ … }}" }` |
| `takes:` `pick:` | draw several takes now; `pick: manual` (default), `first_accepted`, `best: { by: <fact>, order: lowest\|highest }` |
| `assert:` | `[{ check: "${{ … }}", message: "…", on_fail: fail\|skip }]` |
| `at: plan` | run this free, local, deterministic step while planning: its outputs become plan-time values |
| `budget:` | `{ max_usd: N }` for this step, group or each repeat instance (the innermost counts) |
| `concurrency:` | at most N instances of a repeated node step at once (no effect on groups yet) |
| `route:` | which model serves this step (`model@provider`) |
| `requires:` | features the route must support: `image_input`, `mask`, `alpha`, `exact_size` |
| `independent_of:` | refuse a route that shares a model with these steps |
| `timeout:` | seconds; past it the step fails and is not run again |

### Expressions

`${{ … }}` works in any value. A value that is exactly one expression keeps its type (a list stays
a list); inside other text it makes a string. There are no loops, user functions or string methods:
write a node when you need more.

| Write | Example |
|---|---|
| references | `inputs.poster`, `steps.draw.outputs.image`, `steps.review.facts.verdict`, `item.id`, `let.ready`, `tables.rows`, `matrix.eye` |
| one instance | `steps.entity['harbor_keeper'].draw`, `steps.cell[item.eye]` |
| a collection | `steps.entity.*.draw.outputs.image` (ordered like the list, keyed) |
| fields, elements | `steps.propose.outputs.json.entities`, `inputs.layers[0]` |
| operators | `+ - * /`, `== != < <= > >=`, `&&`, `\|\|`, `!` |
| fallback | `a ?? b`: `b` when `a` is null, a skipped step's result, or the last field read is missing |
| file facts | `facts(inputs.poster).width`, `.height`, `.has_alpha`, `.opaque`, `.bytes`, `.kind`; audio `.duration`; video `.width`, `.height`, `.fps`, `.duration`, `.frames` |
| functions | `lookup(map, key)`, `min`, `max`, `len`, `contains`, `concat(a, b)`, `join(list, ", ")`, `stem(file)`, `digest(value)`, `accepted(collection)` |

Names the workflow declares are checked even under `??` (a misspelt input fails). Node facts are
what a step reported (`ctx.fact`), read as `steps.<name>.facts.<fact>`.

### Judges, rejection and regeneration

A judge is a step with `judges: <step>` that reports a `verdict` fact (`accept` or `reject`).
Everything reading the judged step waits for its judges.

| `on_reject:` | |
|---|---|
| `fail` (default) | the judged step fails; its dependents are skipped |
| `continue` | keep the verdict; downstream runs (filter with `accepted(...)`) |
| `skip` | skip downstream of the judged step; the run still succeeds |
| `regenerate: { max: N, then: fail\|continue\|skip\|keep_best: { by: <fact>, order: lowest\|highest }, feedback: true }` | draw again until accepted; `max` counts all takes, the first included |

Three failures stay apart: a failed paid call is retried by the engine (at most 6 attempts, each
reserved and recorded); a broken node result (`ctx.fail`, wrong outputs) fails the step; a valid
result judged wrong becomes a new take only when you asked for regeneration.

### Phases

A `for_each` over a list a step makes cannot be sized while planning: it starts a new phase,
priced at `max:` in the plan and exactly once the list exists. `--yes-up-to N` stops before a
later phase whose worst case would take the run past N; run again with a higher N to continue. To
avoid a phase, compute the list in an `at: plan` step.

## Built-in node types

`grida fx nodes` lists every type; `grida fx nodes <type>` shows its settings, outputs and routes.
Types marked *planned* plan and price but cannot run yet.

| Type | Settings → outputs | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `fx/image.generate@1` | `prompt`, `size` (`WxH` or `auto`), `background` (`auto`, `opaque`, `transparent`), `references`, `vars` → `image` | paid; `references` only on `imagegen@codex` (≤5) and `imagine@grok` (≤3) |
| `fx/image.edit@1` | `image`, `mask`, `references`, `prompt`, `size`, `background` → `image` | paid; masks only on `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst@openai` |
| `fx/structured.generate@1` | `prompt`, `system`, `context` (text, json, images), `schema`, `max_tokens`, `vars` → `json` | paid |
| `fx/video.generate@1` | `prompt`, `first_frame`, `last_frame`, `duration`, `resolution`, `aspect_ratio` → `video` | paid, long job |
| `fx/speech.generate@1` | `text`, `voice`, `stability`, `language_code`, `max_chars` → `audio` | paid |
| `fx/sound.generate@1` | `prompt`, `duration`, `prompt_influence`, `loop` → `audio` | paid |
| `fx/music.generate@1` | `prompt`, `duration` → `audio` | paid |
| `fx/mesh.generate@1` | `views` (`front` plus `back`, `left` or `right`), `face_limit`, `quad`, `texture`, `pbr` → `model` | paid, long job |
| `fx/mesh.rig@1` | `model`, `rig_type`, `skeleton` → `model` (binary glTF) | paid, long job |
| `fx/image.check_alpha@1` | `image`, `expect` (`transparent`, `opaque`) → verdict | free judge (Python) |
| `fx/image.check_size@1` | `image`, `width`, `height` → verdict | free judge (Python) |
| `fx/image.resize@1` | `image`, `longest_side` or `width`/`height` → `image` | free (Python) |
| `fx/image.crop@1` | `image`, `box`, `padding`, or `region` (annotations) → `image` | free (Python) |
| `fx/image.pad@1` | `image`, `width`, `height` → `image` | free (Python) |
| `fx/image.mirror_repeat@1` | `image`, `axis` (`x`, `y`, `xy`) → `image` | free (Python) |
| `fx/select@1` | `first_of: [...]` → the first that exists and was not rejected, under its own port name | free (engine) |
| `fx/json.merge@1` | `documents` → `json` | free (Python) |
| `fx/package@1` | `files` (`"dest/{key}.png": <collection>`), `manifest` → `files`, `manifest` | free (Python) |
| `fx/files.copy@1` | `file` → `file` | free (Python) |
| `fx/background.remove@1` | `image` → `image` | *planned*: no built-in route |
| `fx/vision.annotate@1`, `fx/vision.review@1`, `fx/structured.review@1`, `fx/audio.check_duration@1` | | *planned* |
| `fx/image.compose@1`, `key`, `sheet`, `contact_sheet`; `fx/video.probe@1`, `frames`, `encode`; `fx/audio.normalize@1`, `trim`, `concat`, `mix`; `fx/annotations.mask@1`, `filter` | | *planned* |

Every paid type also takes `provider_options`: parameters FX does not expose, by provider (Routes
and providers, below). A prompt may be a template file (`prompt: ./prompts/draw.md`), rendered with
the step's `vars:` and the workflow's `inputs`. Until `vision.review` runs, a model's judgement is a
`structured.generate` answer read by a judge you write (recipe below).

## Routes and providers

A route is `model@provider`. Pick one per capability in `fx.yaml` `routes:`, or per step with
`route:`. `grida fx nodes <type>` lists routes; `grida fx doctor` says which a live run can serve.

| Capability | Built-in routes | Key |
|---|---|---|
| `image.generate`, `image.edit` | `openai/gpt-image-2.5-sunburst@gg`; `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst@openai`; `openai/gpt-image-2.5-sunburst@openrouter`; `openai/gpt-image-2.5/sunburst@fal`; `imagegen@codex`; `imagine@grok` | `GG_API_KEY`, else the provider's; none for Codex and Grok Build |
| `structured.generate`, `agent.turn` | `openai/gpt-5.6-sol@gg`, `openai/gpt-6-astra@gg`; the same models `@openrouter` | `GG_API_KEY`, else `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` |
| `video.generate` | `alibaba/wan-3.0@gg`; `google/gemini-omni-flash/v1.1/image-to-video@fal` | `GG_API_KEY`, else `FAL_KEY` |
| `mesh.generate`, `mesh.rig` | `tripo/p2@gg`, `tripo/rig-v1.0@gg`; `P2-20260801@tripo`, `v1.0-20240301@tripo` | `GG_API_KEY`, else `TRIPO_API_KEY` |
| `music.generate` | `google/lyria-3-pro-preview@openrouter` | `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` |
| `sound.generate`, `speech.generate` | `eleven_text_to_sound_v2@elevenlabs`, `eleven_v3@elevenlabs` | `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` |

- **Grida Gateway (`@gg`)**: one key, `GG_API_KEY` (from console.grida.co), for text, agent turns,
  images, video and 3D, billed to Grida AI credits; it needs the `text` and `media` scopes.
- **Your own Codex (`imagegen@codex`)** and **your own Grok Build (`imagine@grok`)**: images with no
  API key, counted against the user's own subscription and booked by FX at $0. Neither takes an
  exact `size` (leave it out and resize after) or a `mask`; Grok Build has no transparency. A run
  whose paid calls are all on them needs no ceiling (it runs under $0 and refuses other routes).
- **Keys** come from the environment, else the project's `.env` (only the eleven FX key and base
  URL names are read). Keys never go in `fx.yaml` or a workflow. Without `--live` no key is used.
  `*_BASE_URL` variables point a provider at a proxy; `HTTPS_PROXY`/`ALL_PROXY` are honoured.
  HTTPS trusts the public roots and the platform's certificate store (`SSL_CERT_FILE`/`SSL_CERT_DIR`
  in its place when set), so a proxy whose root the machine trusts works.
- Built-in prices are planning allowances; a call is booked at what the provider reports, else at
  its whole reservation. A route on a provider with no adapter still plans; live it is refused.
- **A route whose price you do not know** takes a cap instead: `price: { cap_usd: N }`, alone in
  `price`. Each call is planned at $0 to N and holds N against the ceiling, and is booked at what
  the provider reports, else at N. The cap is what FX holds, not a limit the provider honours: a
  dearer call is booked in full. The plan text adds a `note` per capped route (not in a stand-in
  run, which holds nothing), and `plan --json` marks each step that calls one with `capped: true`
  in its `price`. A `price` must state an amount: `usd: 0` is free, and `price: {}` is refused.
- **Parameters FX does not expose** go in `provider_options`, an object by provider whose members
  are the provider's own parameters: a paid step's `with:` takes it, and so does a route's
  `contract`. Only the member of the provider the call runs on is sent, after FX's own members; a
  step's parameter replaces the route's of the same name, and other providers' members are kept
  for the routes a step may fall back to. A parameter FX sets itself (`prompt`, `size`, `model`,
  `n`, `stream`, …; each provider's list is in its adapter's reference), and a file, are refused
  before anything is sent, at $0. Codex and Grok Build take none. Options are part of the call's
  identity (another value is another paid call) and are recorded with the run, so never put a key
  in them. An agent run's turns take only their route's: the engine builds each turn's request.

```yaml
    with:
      prompt: Name a colour.
      schema: ./schemas/colour.json
      provider_options:
        openrouter: { seed: 7 }   # read only when the step runs on an @openrouter route
```
- **Your own route table** (`fx: routes/v1`, listed under `route_tables:` in `fx.yaml`): its entry
  for a capability and route replaces the built-in one. An entry may `extends:` another route of
  the same capability and provider, a built-in one (even with `--routes`) or one read before it,
  and state only what differs: it takes the base's price, features, limits, pacing and
  `contract`, a member it states replaces the base's, and `contract` merges member by member.
  `extends` is not part of a route's identity, so repricing a route this way keeps every cache.
  On a provider and capability FX has an adapter for, a `contract` that leaves out `adapter` gets
  FX's, and one that leaves out `adapter_behavior` gets its behaviour unless it names another
  adapter.

```yaml
# routes/prices.yaml
fx: routes/v1
routes:
  - capability: image.generate
    route: openai/gpt-image-2.5-sunburst@gg
    extends: openai/gpt-image-2.5-sunburst@gg   # the built-in entry, with more headroom
    price: { low_usd: 0.09, high_usd: 0.80 }     # replaces its whole price, size tiers included
  - capability: structured.generate
    route: openai/gpt-5.6-sol@openrouter
    extends: openai/gpt-5.6-sol@openrouter
    contract:
      provider_options: { openrouter: { seed: 7 } }   # sent with every call; part of the route's identity
```

- **Upgrading from 0.6.1:** a route of your own on a provider and capability FX has an adapter for,
  whose `contract` left out `adapter`, or named FX's adapter and left out `adapter_behavior`, now
  has them filled in, so its identity changes once: its steps and paid calls run again, and
  resuming a run folder planned before is refused (start a new run). Built-in routes keep theirs.
  A route of your own on `fal` or `tripo` whose `contract` names an `adapter_behavior` other than
  FX's is now refused when a call is sent, as on every other provider. A step whose `requires:`
  names `jpeg_output`, `webp_output` or `hosted_url_reference_input` is now refused while planning
  as no feature of its capability: drop the name, since every route answers PNG and sends input
  pictures inline. A route whose `price` states no amount (`price: {}`, which was $0) is now
  refused: write `usd: 0` for a free route, or `cap_usd` for one whose price you do not know. A
  route of your own whose `contract` already named `provider_options`, which most adapters ignored,
  now sends its provider's member, or is refused when the call is sent if that member sets a
  parameter FX owns (on Codex and Grok Build, if it is not empty); its identity is unchanged, so a
  call cached before still replays without them (`reroll` the step for a new one). One that is not
  an object of objects is now refused while the table is read.

## Your own nodes

A node type in your project is a function with a declaration. Do the work and return the declared
outputs; never write undeclared files, read undeclared files, call providers directly, retry, or
cache: FX does all of that. Without `version`, a node's identity follows its source (the module,
the project modules it imports, declared `resources`), so editing it reruns it; paid calls inside
are still cached by request. With `version=N`, only a bump reruns it; `grida fx lock` pins its
source in `fx.lock`, and `grida fx lock --same <file>#<name>` confirms a change that keeps behaviour.

Declaration fields (Python keyword arguments, TypeScript object members): `inputs` (`"image"`,
`"image[]"` a list, `"image{}"` a keyed collection, trailing `?` optional), `params` (types, a tuple
or list of allowed values, or a JSON Schema), `outputs` (`"image/png"`, `"json"`, `"annotations?"`),
`calls` (`{"image.edit": 1}`: the most paid calls per run, which the plan prices; an undeclared call
fails), `resources` (project files it reads), `tools` (external programs, checked by `doctor`;
`GRIDA_FX_TOOL_<NAME>` picks a build), `judge` (must report a `verdict` fact), `version`, `retry`
(`"engine"`: rerun after an exception, for providers you call your own way).

What `ctx` gives (Python name; TypeScript in camelCase where it differs):

| | |
|---|---|
| `ctx.read.image/json/text/bytes(name)` | a declared input (`image` is PIL; TypeScript has `bytes/text/json`, no image decoding) |
| `ctx.inputs[name]` | the file: `.path`, `.kind`, `.digest`, `.key`, `.facts` |
| `ctx.params` | settings, typed |
| `ctx.out.png/json/text/bytes(...)` | an output value to return; `ctx.out.path(name)` + `ctx.out.file(path)` for files a tool writes |
| `ctx.fact(name, value)` | report a node fact (`await` in TypeScript) |
| `ctx.annotate(shape=…, label=…, …)` | add a mark to an `annotations` output |
| `ctx.image_generate/image_edit/structured_generate(...)`, `ctx.capability(...)` | a paid call through FX: routed, priced, budgeted, cached |
| `ctx.agent(system=…, tools=[…])` | a tool-using model loop; declare `calls={"agent.turn": N}` |
| `ctx.tool("ffmpeg").run([...])` | a declared external program |
| `ctx.prompt(path, **vars)` | render a declared resource with `${{ }}` |
| `ctx.work_path(name)`, `ctx.state` | scratch space and state for this run of the node |
| `ctx.progress(text, fraction)` | live progress |
| `raise ctx.fail(msg)` / `throw ctx.fail(msg)` | a broken result: the step fails with your message |

TypeScript nodes run on Node 24+ with types stripped: ES modules (`"type": "module"`), erasable
syntax only (no `enum`, `namespace`, parameter properties), `.ts` in import paths, package.json
`imports` (`#lib/x.ts`) rather than tsconfig `paths`. `tsc` checks bodies against declarations;
FX never type checks. Return a `Map` for a keyed output. Any other language can implement the node
protocol (JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio, `spec/protocol.md`).

## Running

| Command | |
|---|---|
| `grida fx plan <target> [--inputs f]… [--max-usd N] [--check] [--json] [--expect-cached] [--open]` | expand, check and price; never spends. `--check` exits 1 on problems (use it in CI) |
| `grida fx run <target> [--live] [--max-usd N] [--yes-up-to N] [--deliver out=path]… [--name N \| --resume N \| --run DIR] [--stand-in F#fn] [--open \| --no-view]` | run; free steps always run, paid calls only with `--live` |
| `grida fx inspect <run> [--verify] [--json] [--open]` | a run's summary; a workflow id reads its newest run |
| `grida fx reroll <run> <step-path>` / `grida fx pick <run> <step-path> <take>` | the next take of a step / use a take from now on |
| `grida fx takes list <target>` / `grida fx takes mv <target> <old> <new>` | read or repair `<id>.takes.yaml` |
| `grida fx cancel <run> [--invocation ID] [--wait] [--timeout 30s] [--json]` | cancel one invocation; `inspect <run> --control --json` first |
| `grida fx runs list [--workflow ID] [--json]` / `grida fx runs remove <run>… [--yes]` | list runs / remove runs (preview without `--yes`) |
| `grida fx cache prune [--yes]` | remove what no remaining run names |
| `grida fx export <run> --out DIR [--include-values] [--include-diagnostics] [--json]` | a portable copy of a finished run |
| `grida fx jobs [--forget KEY]` | long provider jobs in the cache |
| `grida fx nodes [type]`, `grida fx schema <target>`, `grida fx doctor [target]` | discovery and readiness |
| `grida fx expand`, `identity`, `price <target>`; `grida fx project <run>`; `grida fx observe <run> [--snapshot]` | JSON for tools |
| `grida fx start [--background] [--port N] [--open]`, `status [--json]`, `stop`, `logs [--lines N]` | the project's local viewer service |
| `grida fx init [dir] [--template NAME] [--list-templates]`, `grida fx lock [--same NODE]… [--check]` | project setup, node version locks |

`<target>` is a workflow file, a workflow id, or a builder (`file.py:build`, `file.ts:build`, with
`--arg name=value`). `<run>` is a run folder, a workflow id, or `WORKFLOW_ID/NAME`.

- **Ceiling.** A live run needs one: `--max-usd`, else the workflow's `budget:`, else `fx.yaml`'s.
  Before every paid call and attempt FX reserves its worst case; a call that would cross the
  ceiling is not made, its step fails, dependents are skipped, and the rest of the run goes on.
- **Runs.** Each run is a folder, `runs/<id>/<date>-<n>/`, with `events.jsonl` (the record),
  `plan.json`, `outputs/` and `files/`. A run ends `ok`, `failed` (naming each failure) or
  `incomplete`. `--name NAME` creates a named run once; `--resume NAME` (same target, inputs and
  options) continues it; `--run DIR` creates or continues a folder. Finished steps come from the
  cache and answered calls replay from the record.
- **Takes.** The first result of a request is take 1. `reroll` and `pick` write
  `<id>.takes.yaml` beside the workflow (commit it); every run reads it.
- **Deliver.** `--deliver icons=out/{key}.png` copies declared outputs after the run, `{key}` per
  element; a missing one makes the command exit non-zero. The viewer's **Download all (.zip)** is
  the same files for a person; agents use `--deliver` or `export`.
- **Exit status.** `0` done; `1` refused or not ok (plan problems, a run not ok, a missing
  delivery); `2` unreadable input or a usage mistake; `130` interrupted or cancelled.
- **Offline checks.** `GRIDA_FX_NETWORK=off` refuses every provider request before sending;
  `GRIDA_FX_DISABLE_DOTENV=1` ignores `.env`.

### From Python and JavaScript

```python
from grida.fx import plan, run

planned = plan("icon", inputs={"name": "copper lantern"})
print(planned.estimate(), planned.problems)
result = run(planned, live=True)               # target, inputs and ceiling from the plan
print(result.ok, result.cost, result.failures) # a failed step does not raise
result.deliver({"icon": "out/icon.png"})
```

```ts
import { plan, run } from "@grida/fx";

const planned = await plan("icon", { inputs: { name: "copper lantern" } });
const result = await run(planned, { live: true });
console.log(result.ok, result.chargedUsd, result.failed);
```

Both raise `PlanRefused` for a refused plan and `FxError` for a run refused before it starts. Also:
`run_async`, `load_run(...)`/`loadRun(...)` (saved records, `snapshot`, `events`, `follow`,
`export`), `cancel`/`inspect_control`, `list_runs`/`remove_runs` (`listRuns`/`removeRuns`).

## Recipes

Each recipe is a complete project: every file is shown with its path in a comment on its first
line (the comment is not part of the file), and CI runs the recipe's `grida fx plan` lines, and
its `grida fx run` lines without `--live`, against those files.

### One transparent icon, drawn again until its background is clear

```yaml
# fx.yaml
fx: project/v1
budget: { max_usd: 5 }
routes:
  image.generate: openai/gpt-image-2.5-sunburst@gg
```

```yaml
# workflows/icon.yaml
fx: workflow/v1
id: icon
title: One item icon
inputs:
  name: { type: string, description: "What the item is" }
steps:
  draw:
    uses: fx/image.generate@1
    with:
      prompt: "A single ${{ inputs.name }} game icon, centered, no text."
      background: transparent
      size: 1024x1024
  clean:
    uses: fx/image.check_alpha@1
    judges: draw
    with: { image: "${{ steps.draw.outputs.image }}", expect: transparent }
    on_reject:
      regenerate: { max: 3 }
outputs:
  icon: ${{ steps.draw.outputs.image }}
```

```sh
grida fx plan icon -- --name "copper lantern"
grida fx run icon --live -- --name "copper lantern"
grida fx inspect icon
```

The plan prices every take regeneration may draw. Running it again changes nothing and costs
nothing; another `--name` draws again.

### Many items from a table, sized locally, packed into a folder

```yaml
# workflows/icons.yaml
fx: workflow/v1
id: icons
title: Item icons
tables:
  items:
    - { id: lantern, look: "a copper lantern" }
    - { id: rope, look: "a coil of hemp rope" }
    - { id: map, look: "a folded sea chart" }
steps:
  icon:
    for_each: ${{ tables.items }}
    key: ${{ item.id }}
    concurrency: 2
    steps:
      draw:
        uses: fx/image.generate@1
        route: imagegen@codex
        with: { prompt: "A game inventory icon of ${{ item.look }}, flat style, no text.", background: transparent }
      small:
        uses: fx/image.resize@1
        with: { image: "${{ steps.draw.outputs.image }}", longest_side: 256 }
      square:
        uses: fx/image.pad@1
        with: { image: "${{ steps.small.outputs.image }}", width: 256, height: 256 }
  pack:
    uses: fx/package@1
    with:
      files:
        "icons/{key}.png": ${{ steps.icon.*.square.outputs.image }}
      manifest:
        items: ${{ tables.items }}
outputs:
  icons: ${{ steps.icon.*.square.outputs.image }}
  files: ${{ steps.pack.outputs.files }}
```

```sh
grida fx plan icons
grida fx run icons --live --deliver icons=out/{key}.png
```

`key:` names instances (`icon['rope']`), so takes and delivered files follow the item when the
table changes. On `imagegen@codex` the size is the route's own: resize and pad locally for an exact
canvas. The run needs no ceiling while every paid call is on Codex.

### A model proposes a list; one image per entry (a second phase)

```json
// schemas/cast.json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "characters": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": { "id": { "type": "string" }, "look": { "type": "string" } },
        "required": ["id", "look"]
      }
    }
  },
  "required": ["characters"]
}
```

```yaml
# workflows/cast.yaml
fx: workflow/v1
id: cast
title: Cast portraits
inputs:
  premise: { type: string }
  max_characters: { type: integer, default: 6, minimum: 1, maximum: 12 }
budget: { max_usd: 8 }
steps:
  propose:
    uses: fx/structured.generate@1
    route: openai/gpt-5.6-sol@gg
    with:
      prompt: "Invent the cast of this story, at most ${{ inputs.max_characters }}: ${{ inputs.premise }}"
      schema: ./schemas/cast.json
  portrait:
    for_each: ${{ steps.propose.outputs.json.characters }}
    key: ${{ item.id }}
    max: ${{ inputs.max_characters }}
    uses: fx/image.generate@1
    route: openai/gpt-image-2.5-sunburst@gg
    with: { prompt: "A portrait of ${{ item.look }}, painted, plain background.", size: 1024x1024 }
outputs:
  cast: ${{ steps.propose.outputs.json }}
  portraits: ${{ steps.portrait.*.outputs.image }}
```

```sh
grida fx plan cast -- --premise "a lighthouse keeper's last winter"
grida fx run cast --live --yes-up-to 5 -- --premise "a lighthouse keeper's last winter"
```

Phase 2 is priced at `max:` in the plan, then exactly once `propose` answers. `--yes-up-to 5`
stops before a phase that would take the run past $5.

### Your own Python node and judge

```python
# nodes/tiles.py
from PIL import Image, ImageOps

from grida.fx import Ctx, node


@node("mirror_tile", inputs={"image": "image"}, outputs={"image": "image/png"})
def mirror_tile(ctx: Ctx) -> dict:
    src = ctx.read.image("image")
    out = Image.new(src.mode, (src.width * 2, src.height))
    out.paste(src, (0, 0))
    out.paste(ImageOps.mirror(src), (src.width, 0))
    return {"image": ctx.out.png(out)}


@node("wide_enough", inputs={"image": "image"}, params={"min_width": int}, judge=True)
def wide_enough(ctx: Ctx) -> dict:
    width = ctx.inputs["image"].facts["width"]
    ctx.fact("width", width)
    ctx.fact("verdict", "accept" if width >= ctx.params["min_width"] else "reject")
    return {}
```

```yaml
# workflows/strip.yaml
fx: workflow/v1
id: strip
title: Seamless strip
inputs:
  scene: { type: string }
steps:
  draw:
    uses: fx/image.generate@1
    route: openai/gpt-image-2.5-sunburst@gg
    with: { prompt: "${{ inputs.scene }}, side view, flat colours", size: 1536x1024 }
  tile:
    uses: ./nodes/tiles.py#mirror_tile
    with: { image: "${{ steps.draw.outputs.image }}" }
  wide:
    uses: ./nodes/tiles.py#wide_enough
    judges: tile
    with: { image: "${{ steps.tile.outputs.image }}", min_width: 2048 }
    on_reject: continue
outputs:
  strip: ${{ steps.tile.outputs.image }}
```

```sh
grida fx plan strip --max-usd 2 -- --scene "a harbour at dusk"
```

Python nodes need Python 3.11+ with `grida` (Pillow comes with it). A param declared as a type
(`int`) is checked when the step runs.

### Your own TypeScript node, run offline

```json
// package.json
{ "type": "module", "private": true, "dependencies": { "@grida/fx": "0.6.1" } }
```

```ts
// nodes/palette.ts
import { node } from "@grida/fx";

export const palette = node(
  {
    name: "palette",
    params: { base: "string", steps: { type: "integer", default: 4, minimum: 2 }, mood: ["warm", "cool"] },
    outputs: { swatches: "json" },
  },
  async (ctx) => {
    const swatches = Array.from({ length: ctx.params.steps }, (_, i) => `${ctx.params.base}/${ctx.params.mood}/${i}`);
    await ctx.fact("count", swatches.length);
    return { swatches: ctx.out.json(swatches) };
  },
);
```

```yaml
# workflows/palette.yaml
fx: workflow/v1
id: palette
title: A palette
inputs:
  base: { type: string, default: teal }
steps:
  colours:
    uses: ./nodes/palette.ts#palette
    with: { base: "${{ inputs.base }}", steps: 5, mood: cool }
outputs:
  swatches: ${{ steps.colours.outputs.swatches }}
```

```sh
grida fx plan palette
grida fx run palette -- --base coral
```

`uses:` names the export (`#palette`). Node 24+ runs the `.ts` file as it is; `npm install
@grida/fx` puts the SDK in `node_modules`. Nothing here is paid, so the run needs no `--live`.

### A builder: a workflow from your own data, in Python

```python
# build_icons.py
from grida.fx import Workflow

ITEMS = {"lantern": "a copper lantern", "rope": "a coil of hemp rope"}


def build(theme: str = "flat") -> Workflow:
    wf = Workflow("built-icons", title=f"Icons, {theme}")
    icons = wf.step(
        "icon",
        for_each=[{"id": key, "look": look} for key, look in ITEMS.items()],
        key="${{ item.id }}",
        uses="fx/image.generate@1",
        route="imagegen@codex",
        with_={"prompt": f"A {theme} game icon of ${{{{ item.look }}}}, no text."},
    )
    wf.outputs(icons=icons.all.outputs.image)
    return wf
```

```sh
grida fx plan build_icons.py:build --arg theme=pixel
```

A builder runs while planning and returns the workflow; FX never runs arbitrary scripts to find
one. In TypeScript: `export function build() { return workflow({ id, title, steps, outputs }) }`
with `expr("item.id")` for expressions, planned as `grida fx plan workflows/icons.ts:build`.

### Fall back to another route when a judge rejects

```yaml
# workflows/fallback.yaml
fx: workflow/v1
id: fallback
title: A cut-out, from a second route if needed
inputs:
  subject: { type: string }
steps:
  first:
    uses: fx/image.generate@1
    route: openai/gpt-image-2.5-sunburst@gg
    with: { prompt: "${{ inputs.subject }}, isolated", background: transparent, size: 1024x1024 }
  clear:
    uses: fx/image.check_alpha@1
    judges: first
    with: { image: "${{ steps.first.outputs.image }}", expect: transparent }
    on_reject: continue
  second:
    if: ${{ steps.clear.facts.verdict == 'reject' }}
    uses: fx/image.generate@1
    route: imagegen@codex
    with: { prompt: "${{ inputs.subject }}, isolated", background: transparent }
  chosen:
    uses: fx/select@1
    with: { first_of: ["${{ steps.first.outputs.image }}", "${{ steps.second.outputs.image }}"] }
outputs:
  picture: ${{ steps.chosen.outputs.image }}
```

```sh
grida fx plan fallback --max-usd 1 -- --subject "a brass key"
```

`second` depends on a run-time verdict, so the plan prices it as *maybe*. `select` skips
candidates whose step was skipped or rejected; `a ?? b` does the same for a skipped step's result.

### Test a workflow offline with a stand-in

```python
# tests/stand_in.py
import io

from PIL import Image

from grida.fx import DECLINE, Answer


def answer(call):
    if call.capability != "image.generate":
        return DECLINE
    width, height = map(int, call.request["size"].split("x"))
    picture = Image.new("RGBA", (width, height), (0, 0, 0, 0))
    picture.paste((200, 120, 40, 255), (width // 4, height // 4, width * 3 // 4, height * 3 // 4))
    out = io.BytesIO()
    picture.save(out, "PNG")
    return Answer(files={"image": out.getvalue()})
```

```yaml
# workflows/icon.yaml
fx: workflow/v1
id: icon
title: One item icon
inputs:
  name: { type: string }
steps:
  draw:
    uses: fx/image.generate@1
    route: openai/gpt-image-2.5-sunburst@gg
    with: { prompt: "A ${{ inputs.name }} icon, no text.", background: transparent, size: 1024x1024 }
  clean:
    uses: fx/image.check_alpha@1
    judges: draw
    with: { image: "${{ steps.draw.outputs.image }}", expect: transparent }
outputs:
  icon: ${{ steps.draw.outputs.image }}
```

```sh
grida fx plan icon -- --name lantern
grida fx run icon --stand-in tests/stand_in.py#answer -- --name lantern
```

A stand-in answers paid calls with your function: offline, for nothing, checked as a provider's
answer would be (a picture of the wrong size fails the call). It keeps its own cache
(`.fx/cache/stand-in/`), never mixes with paid answers, and cannot be combined with `--live` or
`--yes-up-to`. Return `Answer(...)`, `DECLINE` (the call fails as not live), or raise
`CallRefused`/`CallFailed`; anything else stops the run. From the SDKs: `run(..., stand_in=fn)` in
Python, `run(..., { standIn: fn })` in JavaScript, in your own process.

## When something fails

| You see | Do |
|---|---|
| `"title" is a required property` | a workflow needs `fx`, `id`, `title` and `steps` |
| `plain scalar 'on' is ambiguous …; quote it` | quote the value (`"on"`, `"16:9"`, `"2026-10-05"`) |
| `inputs: 'name' is a required property` | give the input: `-- --name …` or `--inputs file.yaml` |
| `… is a paid call; run with --live` | the step needs a provider: ask the user, then `--live` with a ceiling |
| `refused: a live run needs a ceiling: …` | add `--max-usd N` (agreed with the user) or a `budget:` |
| `… was refused: GG_API_KEY is not set` | the user sets the key (environment or `.env`); check with `grida fx doctor` |
| `<route> does not support exact_size` (or `alpha`, `mask`, `image_input`) | change the setting or the route; for Codex and Grok Build leave `size` out and resize after |
| `no adapter serves <route> …` | FX cannot call that provider; pick a built-in route (`grida fx nodes <type>`) |
| `routes.<n>.extends: no route <base> serves <capability>` | `extends` names a route of the same capability declared earlier (in the same table or one read before) or a built-in one; check the id and the order |
| `routes.<n>.extends: <base> is not a <provider> route` | a route extends only a route of its own provider |
| `routes.<n>.price: a price states an amount (usd, low_usd, high_usd) or a cap (cap_usd)` | give the route its price, or `cap_usd: N` when its price is not known; an empty `price` is not $0 |
| `routes.<n>.price: {…} has more than 1 property` | `cap_usd` stands alone in `price`: drop the other members |
| `… was refused: provider_options.<provider>.<name> is a member FX owns` (or `contract.provider_options…`) | FX sets that parameter itself: use the type's own setting, or leave it out |
| `… was refused: provider_options.<provider>.<name> holds a file: provider options are JSON only` (or `provider_options.<provider> holds a file…`) | pass files through the type's inputs; options carry JSON only |
| `… was refused: Codex takes no provider_options` (or `Grok Build …`) | drop `provider_options.codex` (or `.grok`); other providers' members may stay |
| `routes.<n>.contract.provider_options.<provider>: … is not of type "object"` | write `provider_options: { <provider>: { <parameter>: <value> } }` |
| `not installed (codex)` / `not installed (grok)` in doctor | install and sign in to Codex or Grok Build, or set `GRIDA_FX_TOOL_CODEX` / `GRIDA_FX_TOOL_GROK` |
| `Codex … is older than 0.160.1` (or `too old (codex …)` in doctor) | update the Codex that doctor's `program` line names, or set `GRIDA_FX_TOOL_CODEX` to a newer one |
| `python … too old` / `no grida` in doctor | `uv sync` or `pip install grida` in the project, or set `GRIDA_FX_PYTHON` |
| `node … too old` / `no @grida/fx` | Node 24+, `npm install @grida/fx`, or set `GRIDA_FX_NODE` |
| `take <n> of <path> no longer produces the picked result …` | the request changed since the pick: `grida fx pick` or `reroll` again |
| `stopped   phase 2 may cost up to $…` | the next phase needs approval: run again with a higher `--yes-up-to` |
| a versioned node's source changed | bump `version`, or `grida fx lock --same <file>#<name>` |
| `port 8787 is in use` | `grida fx start --background --port <N>` |
| a `submitting` job in `grida fx jobs` | check the provider's dashboard, then `grida fx jobs --forget <key>` |
